chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Aban from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, 'One who has dyed (his hair) does not go to bed with his wife.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, why does one who has dyed not go to bed with his wife?' He said, 'Because he is confined.'

key_terms.يُجَامِعُ: to have marital intercourse / go to bed with

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marital intercourse for a man who has dyed his hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a man with dyed hair is prohibited from marital intercourse because he is considered *muhtasar* (restricted or confined). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that specific physical adornments can create a temporary state of ritual or legal restriction, emphasizing the connection between outward appearance and intimate marital conduct.
